answer: Divergent-Fork Challenge: each epoch a quartz beacon selects a checkpoint and jade nonce; agents publish a signed fork hash from their local state, queued via a jetty scheduler. Exact clones share state, so they emit identical fork hashes and are clustered/revoked. To pass as distinct, an attacker must maintain a separately diverging execution history and storage per sybil, paying full compute and state costs; copied identities collide.
